theater: 山東鄒平長白山至濟北

battle.name: 王薄起義
battle.theater: 山東鄒平長白山至濟北
battle.brief: 大業七年（611）冬，山東鄒平長白山下，王薄聚眾起兵，以《無向隍頭望故鄉》為號，眾至數萬，劫掠州郡，與河北張金稱部遙相呼應。隋廷集兵百餘萬於涿郡，山東守備空虛，遣將討之，數月眾潰，王薄下落不明。卡面的科林斯青銅盔出自西元前七世紀的希臘，只能對照：護身的是身邊站著的人，不是那頂盔。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 交戰的兩方是隋朝官軍與山東起義集團。隋朝一方的兵制在隋文帝朝已經改變：府兵制瓦解之後，京師禁軍（左右武衛、翊衛等）、各州郡臨時徵發的鄉兵，以及按資糧雇募的募兵並存，另有北方沿邊州郡的蕃騎與降附部眾可用。大業七年秋，隋廷在河北道北端的涿郡、幽州一線集中兵力，準備翌年再征高句麗，能抽調往山東的精兵因此有限；山東各縣留下的，多是剛從田間抽出的丁壯，既無訓練也無器械，缺糧、缺械、缺冬衣。起義一方並非編制完整的軍隊，而是以同鄉、姻族、符信與歌辭串連起來的散眾，核心是長白山周邊的鄉民、獵戶、逃戶與被徵而未赴軍的丁壯，首領之下是數個互不隸屬的小股，平日各自劫掠，遇官軍則合則散。第三方是同期在其他地區起事的力量：河北有張金稱、高士達、孫安祖等部，江南有高智慧等部，彼此以響應、互援與官軍的兵力調度相互牽動。北方邊地，契丹、靺鞨往來於塞外，隋廷在同年秋又因雁門被突厥圍困而向天下募兵，令齊魯與河北的郡縣再出一層力。整個北方因此處於守備抽空的狀態：能打仗的兵在幽州與遼東，能運糧的船與車在河北道上，能守住縣城的只剩下倉促集合的鄉兵。
countriesEn: The two sides were the armies of the Sui court and the insurgent bands of Shandong. The military system on the Sui side had already been changed under Emperor Wen: with the fubing system broken down, the capital guards (the Left and Right Wuwei formations, the Yiwei and the rest), the levies hastily raised by each prefecture and county, and soldiers hired against payment and rations all existed side by side, together with the tribal horsemen and the surrendered peoples available on the northern frontier commanderies. In the autumn of Daye 7 the court concentrated its strength on the Zhuojun and Youzhou line at the northern end of the Hebei circuit, preparing the renewed campaign against Goguryeo in the year to come, and the seasoned troops that could be sent to Shandong were accordingly few; what was left behind in the counties of Shandong was mostly men taken out of the fields a moment before, without training and without equipment, short of grain, arms and winter clothing. The insurgent side was not an army with an order of battle at all but a loose public held together by kinship, marriage ties, written talismans and songs; the core was the villagers, hunters, absentees and conscripts not yet gone to the colours around Mount Changbai, and beneath the leader there were several mutually independent bands that plundered on their own and, when government troops came, either merged or scattered. Third parties were the movements rising elsewhere at the same time: Zhang Jincheng, Gao Shida and Sun Anzu in Hebei, Gao Zhihui and others in Jiangnan, each of them tied to the others by mutual answering, by reinforcement and by the movement of government troops. On the northern frontier the Khitan and the Mohe passed in and out beyond the passes, and in the same autumn the court had to summon troops from every commandery when the Turks besieged Yanmen, which drew one more layer of men out of the counties of Qi and Lu and of Hebei. The whole of the north was therefore in a state of hollowed defence: the soldiers who could fight were in Youzhou and Liaodong, the wagons and boats that could carry grain were on the Hebei circuit, and the men left to hold the county towns were no more than hastily mustered villagers.
people: 史籍為此役留下的人名極少，可以確定的是以下幾位。王薄是起義的直接首領，齊州鄒平縣長白山一帶的民間人物，《隋書·炀帝紀》只以「河北有民王薄」一句定其身分，既無官職也無家世記載；他的出身大致是漁獵或耕作的鄉民，具體年齡與生平無從查考。他聚眾之後所作的《無向隍頭望故鄉》成為起義的旗號，鄉里傳唱，遠近應和，遂成眾至數萬之勢；他不是受過軍事訓練的統帥，起義過程中沒有建立穩定的編制，也沒有可守的都城，兵眾靠的是歌辭與鄉里關係維繫。隋煬帝楊廣是這一局面的推手，大業七年冬他已移駕涿郡，準備翌年東征，詔天下兵百餘萬，長子供食、官給作者；這道徵發令把山東、河北的丁壯、役夫與糧秣一併抽向北方，鄉村只剩老弱。張須暱是同年秋末雁門被突厥圍困的主將，兵敗被圍，朝廷詔天下募兵赴援，郡縣之兵於是再抽一層，離開鄉里的壯丁更多。宇文述與于仲文等宿將統率的是幽州方向的大軍，與山東起義並不在同一條戰線上。河北的張金稱、高士達、孫安祖與王薄同年起事，東西相應；此後竇建德起於涿郡、杜伏威起於江淮，而王薄本人於起義被平之後下落不明，舊史沒有留下他的結局。
peopleEn: The histories leave very few names for this rising, and the following are the ones that can be established. Wang Bo was the immediate leader of the rising, a commoner from the neighbourhood of Mount Changbai in Zouping county of Qizhou; the Suishu, in the annals of Emperor Yangdi, fixes his identity with a single phrase, that there was a man of Hebei named Wang Bo, and records neither office nor family, so that his background was broadly a villager who fished, hunted or tilled, with no trace of his age or his life beyond that. The song he composed after gathering his followers, the Song of Not Looking toward the Longtou for Home, became the banner of the rising; it was sung through the villages and answered from near and far, and the host grew to several tens of thousands. He was not a commander trained in war: no stable organisation was built during the rising, no capital city was held, and the host was held together by song and by village relationships. Emperor Yangdi of Sui, Yang Guang, was the force behind the situation; in the winter of Daye 7 he had already moved his court to Zhuojun in preparation for the campaign east in the following year, and issued the edict mustering more than a million men from throughout the realm, with the emperor himself providing the food and the government the artisans; that levy drew the able-bodied men, the porters and the grain of Shandong and Hebei northwards at one stroke, leaving only the old and the weak in the villages. Zhang Xuni was the commander besieged by the Turks at Yanmen in the late autumn of the same year; he was beaten and shut in, the court summoned troops from everywhere to relieve him, and the levies of the counties were drawn away once more, so that still more men left their villages. Yuwen Shu, Yu Zhongwen and the other seasoned commanders led the great army on the Youzhou front, which was not on the same line of operations as the rising in Shandong. In Hebei, Zhang Jincheng, Gao Shida and Sun Anzu rose in the same year and answered the rising from the east; later Dou Jiande rose at Zhuojun and Du Fuwei in the Jianghuai, while Wang Bo himself disappeared after the rising was put down, and the old histories preserve no account of his end.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯青銅盔是西元前七世紀希臘的產物：全正面開眼，眼孔與鼻樑連為一體，只留口部與下緣的開口，戴上之後視界極窄，行動與呼吸都受限制；它必須配合密集的方陣才有意義，離了隊形便只剩重量。這件裝備與六一一年山東的戰場相隔一千二百六十餘年，不可能在長白山下出現；它在此只能當作一面對照的鏡子。義軍的裝備極為簡陋，多半是農具與獵具改造而成：削尖的竹木長桿、柴刀、耒耜一類的短兵、獵弓與自製的箭、漁叉，少數骨幹才有從陣亡官軍身上繳來的零散甲片與兜鍪，皮甲只在個別首領身上出現，沒有制式的鎧甲，也沒有攻城器械，糧食則靠就地取給與劫掠糧倉。隋朝官軍的裝備則自成體系：明光甲與札甲，披玄甲的重騎兵用於追擊與壓制，步卒持槊、長刀與劍，遠程以腰弩、擘張弩與角弓為主，攻取城邑另有雲梯、砲車與水攻之具；馬匹在山東與河北向來不缺，郡縣的廄牧與北苑牧馬是騎兵行動的基礎。運輸方面，官軍靠牛車、馬車與驛傳轉輸糧秣，義軍則以人力肩挑與搶來的牛車轉運，一方靠制度，一方靠搶奪，這正是兩者在持久戰中分出勝負的地方。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is a product of seventh-century Greece: the face is open all the way across, the eye openings and the nasal are formed in one piece, and only the mouth and the lower edge are left open, so that once it is worn the field of view is extremely narrow and both movement and breathing are restricted. It only makes sense in company with a dense phalanx; away from the formation it is nothing but weight. This equipment stands about one thousand two hundred and sixty years away from the battlefield in Shandong in 611 and could not have appeared under Mount Changbai; here it can only serve as a mirror for comparison. The arms of the insurgents were extremely simple, most of them agricultural and hunting tools turned to other use: sharpened bamboo and wooden poles, wood-axes, short weapons cut from mattocks, hunting bows with home-made arrows, and fish-spears; only a few of the core men had any armour at all, a few scattered plates and a helmet taken from government soldiers who had fallen, and leather armour appeared on isolated leaders alone. There were no made-up suits of armour and no siege engines, and food was taken from the spot or seized from granaries. The equipment of the Sui armies formed a system of its own: mingguang and zhajia armour, heavy cavalry wearing black armour used for pursuit and for shock, infantry carrying long spears, long sabres and swords, and for the range the waist-mounted crossbow, the shoulder-drawn crossbow and the horn bow, while the taking of walled towns was done with scaling ladders, stone-throwing trebuchots and the use of water. Horses were never scarce in Shandong and Hebei, and the stallions of the county remounts and of the northern imperial pastures were the basis of the cavalry's movement. In the matter of transport, the government moved grain on ox carts, horse carts and the courier relay, while the insurgents shifted it on human shoulders and on stolen ox carts; one side relied on institutions, the other on plunder, and that was precisely where the two sides separated over a war of endurance.
tactics: 起義的戰法幾乎沒有留下文字，只能從結果與當時的條件反推。王薄部的做法大體是鄉民自衛的延伸：以長白山一帶的山地、丘陵與村社為依託，結伙流動，晝伏夜出，選擇郡縣守備空虛、驛傳斷絕、倉廩有存的時段攻入，奪取糧食、衣物與牲畜，得手即散，避開官軍搜索的鋒頭，退回山中重新集結；聯絡靠歌辭與符信，聽得懂那支歌、認得那張符的便是自己人。官軍的應對則不追求野戰決勝，而以據點與封控取勝：據城固守、封鎖出山路口、以弩手覆蓋隘口、派騎兵巡搜山道，同時從後方轉輸糧秣，逼迫義軍在山中斷糧；由於精兵主力集中在涿郡與幽州，能投入山東的兵力必須分批使用，於是一次只能剿一處，也就無法同時壓住齊魯平原上同時冒出的響應者。冬春之交是義軍最難熬的時段：山東丘陵地帶的夜里滴水成冰，起義者多無棉衣、無鞋，糧食靠搶，吃不上就散，一場寒潮或一場雨雪就能讓整支隊伍瓦解。雙方的較量因此不是陣法與裝備的較量，而是流動與封鎖、飢寒與後勤的較量；起義部在這一點上先垮了下去。科林斯青銅盔的教訓在這裡也恰好成立：全套防護要靠整支隊伍與整套後勤來養，一支靠臨時湊起來的隊伍戴上一頂盔，也只是讓人跑得更慢。
tacticsEn: The method of the rising left almost no written trace and can only be reconstructed from its results and from the conditions of the time. The practice of Wang Bo's bands was in effect an extension of village self-defence: they relied on the hills, the ridges and the village communities around Mount Changbai, moved in bands, lay hidden by day and struck by night, and chose their moments when a county garrison was thin, the courier relay broken and the granaries full, seizing grain, clothing and cattle, breaking off as soon as they had it, keeping away from the point of the government's search and withdrawing into the hills to gather again. Their liaison was by song and by talisman: whoever knew the song and recognised the paper was one of them. The government's answer did not aim at winning a battle in the open but at winning by holding points and sealing the country: it sat in the towns, blocked the passes out of the mountains, covered the defiles with crossbowmen, sent cavalry to sweep the mountain paths, and at the same time moved grain up from behind, so as to starve the insurgents out of the hills. Since the seasoned troops were concentrated at Zhuojun and Youzhou, the force that could be put into Shandong had to be used in dribs and drabs; one place could be crushed at a time, and no one could hold down at once the answers that were springing up all over the plain of Qi and Lu. The turn of winter and spring was the hardest stretch for the insurgents: the nights in the hills of Shandong froze hard, most of the rebels had no padded jacket and no shoes, their food was whatever they could take, and when they could not eat they dispersed, so that a single cold snap or a single fall of sleet could dissolve a whole company. The contest between the two sides was therefore not a contest of formation and equipment but a contest of movement against blockade, of hunger and cold against logistics; and on that ground the insurgents broke first. The lesson of the Corinthian helmet fits the moment exactly: a complete set of protection has to be kept up by the whole company and by a whole logistics system, and a force improvised from the ground puts a helmet on its men only to make them slower.
data: 可核實的數字並不多，以下幾項大致可靠。時間軸：大業七年（611）冬起兵，同年秋末雁門被突厥圍困，隋廷詔天下募兵；大業八年（612）正月，宇文述等率三十萬五千人渡河征高句麗；大業九年（613），起事已蔓延到二十餘州；其後瓦崗、竇建德、杜伏威各據一方，至大業十三年與武德元年間隋室傾覆。起義本身的規模，《隋書》記為「眾至數萬，劫掠州郡」，可以確定是數萬之眾，而不是史書偶爾夸大的百萬；所謂「百餘萬」是大業七年集兵涿郡的全國總徵發數，兩者不可混為一談。背景數字中可引用的，是第一次征高句麗「天下兵百餘萬，長子供食、官給作者」的記載，以及翌年出師時三十萬五千人渡河的數目，兩者說明隋朝把全國兵力的重心壓在東北，因而山東的防守必然空虛。地理上，長白山在齊州鄒平縣，即今山東省淄博市鄒平區長白鎮一帶，距濟南府城約百餘里，義軍在濟水與黃河之間的平原與丘陵上活動，縱深不過數百里，一日之內可達數縣。本役的戰果與死傷沒有留下可靠數字：舊史只留下起兵、被討、眾散、王薄下落不明幾個結果，雙方損耗均無可核對；周圍將領傳中「斬首數千級」「擒獲數萬」一類數字屢見，但沒有任何一條明確屬於王薄之役，不可以套用。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are scarce, and the following are broadly reliable. The time axis: the rising began in the winter of Daye 7 (611); in the same late autumn the Turks besieged Yanmen and the court summoned troops from all over; in the first month of Daye 8 (612) Yuwen Shu and the others led thirty and five thousand men across the river against Goguryeo; by Daye 9 (613) the risings had spread to more than twenty commanderies; afterwards Wagang, Dou Jiande and Du Fuwei each held a region of their own, and the Sui house came down between Daye 13 and the first year of Wude. As for the size of the rising itself, the Suishu records it as 'the host reaching several tens of thousands, plundering commanderies and counties', so that a host of several tens of thousands is certain and it was not the hundred thousands that the histories occasionally exaggerate to; the 'more than a million' figure belongs to the general muster at Zhuojun in Daye 7 and the two numbers must not be run together. Among the background figures that can be quoted are the account of the first campaign against Goguryeo, that 'more than a million men were mustered from throughout the realm, with the emperor providing the food and the government the artisans', and the number of thirty and five thousand crossing the river when the army set out the following year; both show that the Sui had thrown the weight of its manpower to the north-east, so that the defence of Shandong was necessarily hollow. Geographically, Mount Changbai lies in Zouping county of Qizhou, that is around Changbai town in Zouping district of Binzhou in present-day Shandong, about a hundred li from the city of Jinan, and the insurgents operated across the plain and the hills between the Ji and the Yellow River, a depth of no more than several hundred li, so that several counties lay within a day's march of one another. The results of the fighting and the losses leave no reliable figures: the old histories preserve only the bare facts of the rising, of its suppression, of the dispersal of the host and of Wang Bo's disappearance, and the losses of both sides cannot be checked; the figures of the sort that appear in the neighbouring biographies, 'several thousand heads cut off' or 'tens of thousands captured', recur constantly, but not one of them is expressly attached to Wang Bo's rising and none of them may be borrowed for it.
cause: 起義的成因可以分成遠近兩層。遠的一層是隋朝自文帝末年以來積累的社會負擔：租調之外雜斂日重，力役與兵役同時加在丁身之上，修河、造龍舟、營建東都與洛陽、巡行天下，一次次把役夫與車馬抽空鄉村；大業年間三巡江都、兩幸北塞，往返之際沿途供億，地方不堪其擾。更深的一層是兵制變化帶來的後果：文帝朝把府兵改為募兵，農民一旦離籍當兵便失去土地與生產，州縣的鄉兵只具名額而無訓練，國家常備的精兵又遠在邊鎮與京師之間，地方守備就只剩這些空架子。近的一層非常具體：大業七年是第一次征高句麗的徵發年，隋廷在涿郡、幽州一線集兵百餘萬，山東、河北正是最近的徵兵區與糧源區，役夫、戰馬與糧秣沿河北道北運，鄉村的丁壯大量被抽走，農事失管；同年秋雁門被圍，朝廷又向各郡募兵解圍，加了一層抽調；入冬之後寒潮與缺糧成了鄉里最直接的壓力。吏治也在加壓：州縣官吏以催督租調為名加派雜稅、動用刑罰，豪強兼併土地與戶口，歉收之歲照收不誤。在這樣的局面下，民間對三征高句麗的不滿早已流傳，只等待有人先動手；王薄在長白山下聚眾，用一支歌把不向隴頭望故鄉的怨望變成了集合的暗號，於是起義得以成立。
causeEn: The causes of the rising can be divided into a near and a far layer. The far layer is the weight the Sui had been accumulating since the end of Emperor Wen's reign: exactions grew heavier alongside the regular levies and taxes, labour and military service fell at the same time upon the able-bodied, and the digging of channels, the building of the great ships, the construction of the eastern and western capitals and the tours of the realm drained villages of porters, wagons and draught animals one time after another; through the Daye years the emperor toured the south three times and the northern frontier twice, and the immense provisioning of the route left the localities unable to bear it. Deeper still are the consequences of the change in the military system: under Emperor Wen the fubing had been replaced by hired troops, so that a peasant who left his register to serve lost both his land and his means of production; the county levies existed as quotas without training, and the state's seasoned soldiers stood far off at the frontier and in the capital, so that local defence was left with nothing but these hollow shells. The near layer is very concrete: Daye 7 was the year of the great levy for the first campaign against Goguryeo. The court mustered more than a million men on the Zhuojun and Youzhou line, and Shandong and Hebei, the nearest districts of recruitment and of supply, supplied the porters, the war horses and the grain that went north along the Hebei circuit, so that huge numbers of village men were taken away and the fields went untended; in the same autumn the siege of Yanmen brought yet another levy, summoned from every commandery to relieve it; and with the onset of winter the cold and the shortage of grain became the sharpest pressure on the countryside. The magistracy added its own: officials levied miscellaneous taxes under the pretext of pressing the regular levies and used the lash, powerful families swallowed land and households, and in a bad harvest year the collection went on as before. Under such conditions the resentment of the countryside over the three campaigns against Goguryeo had long been spreading, and all that was needed was for someone to move first. Wang Bo gathered his followers under Mount Changbai and turned a song into the password of the gathering, and so the rising was able to exist at all.
impact: 王薄起義的意義，首先在於它把隋末亂世的時間線定了下來。此後的史書把大業七年視為民變的起點之一：王薄在山東、張金稱與高士達在河北、高智慧在江南，幾處同時燃起，而原先互不相干的鄉民一旦有了歌號與符信作為聯絡的手段，響應的速度便快得多；到大業九年，起事已遍及二十餘州，隋廷對每一處都要分兵，而分兵正是它兵力不足的根源。制度上的後果同樣深遠：為鎮壓各地起義，隋朝把兵權進一步收到州郡與行軍總管之手，以募兵與鎮守代替已廢的府兵，地方上則大量出現以首領為核心的私屬部曲，國家的軍隊與豪強的部眾界線日漸模糊；唐承隋制，卻不得不改用募兵、倚重方鎮，河北與山東的尚武之風與藩鎮割據的雛形，都可以在隋末這一代的鄉民起義裡找到源頭。經濟上的代價是元氣盡喪：山東、河北大量丁壯脫離農事，漕運與軍需體系崩壞，隋朝在財政與戰爭能力上加速枯竭，縱有百萬之師也無糧可用。文獻上，王薄所作的這支歌被後世視為隋唐民間歌辭中最早的起義歌之一，與敦煌詩卷中的民間歌辭同屬一類，標誌著亂世之中民間自己的聲音開始被記錄、被流傳。
impactEn: The significance of Wang Bo's rising lies first of all in the fact that it set the timeline of the chaos at the end of the Sui. The histories written afterwards treat Daye 7 as one of the starting points of the rebellions: Wang Bo in Shandong, Zhang Jincheng and Gao Shida in Hebei, Gao Zhihui in Jiangnan, several places alight at once, and once villagers who had had no connexion with one another possessed songs, passwords and talismans by which to keep in touch, the speed of the answering rose sharply; by Daye 9 the risings covered more than twenty commanderies, and the court had to divide its troops to meet every one of them, and that division of troops was precisely the root of its shortage. The institutional consequences ran deep as well: to put down the risings in every quarter the Sui drew military authority further into the hands of the commanderies and the mobile commanders, replacing the defunct fubing with hired soldiers and with garrison duty, while in the localities private bands gathered around leaders multiplied, and the line between the armies of the state and the dependants of the powerful grew ever blurrier. The Tang inherited the Sui institutions but had to rely much more heavily on hired soldiers and on the regional commands, and the martial temper of Hebei and Shandong and the embryo of the separatist military governors can both be traced back to the peasant risings of the last Sui generation. The economic cost was exhaustion: great numbers of men in Shandong and Hebei left the fields, the transport system and the military supply system broke down, and the Sui drained away in fiscal and military capacity faster and faster, so that it could muster a million men and have no grain to feed them. In the literature, the song Wang Bo wrote came to be regarded as one of the earliest recorded rising songs of the popular literature of the Sui and Tang, of a kind with the folk songs of the Dunhuang manuscripts, and it marks the point at which the voice of the common people in a time of disorder began to be written down and to be passed on.
result: 就大業七年這一季而言，結果是清楚而迅速的：隋廷遣將率官軍入山搜討，斷其糧道、封其出入，數月之間眾散，王薄本人下落不明，正史與《資治通鑑》都沒有留下他此後的結局，也沒有留下本役的戰報、俘獲或死傷數字；可以確定的只有起兵、被討、平定三個事實。對隋朝而言，這場起義是一次成功的鎮壓，卻不是一次解決：它證明鄉民可以用一支歌在數旬之間聚起數萬人，也證明隋朝的兵制無法在同一時間壓住齊魯、河北、江南多處的響應，而正因為鎮壓成功，各地的起事得以在隋廷注意力集中於北方時接連發生，大業九年已是二十餘州並反，到大業十年前後便出現瓦崗、竇建德、杜伏威、劉黑悶等割據政權，隋室在這些力量之間維持到武德元年才正式傾覆。卡面上的科林斯青銅盔放在這裡恰好合適：那是西元前七世紀的希臘工藝，全正面開眼，戴它的人只能靠隊形活；六一一年山東的起義者沒有盔，卻有一支歌與同鄉的關係，同樣是一種群體的防護。差別只在於，隋朝這時已經沒有制度能夠把這樣的隊伍編入任何編制之中。
resultEn: For that season of Daye 7 the outcome was clear and swift: the court sent generals with government troops into the mountains to hunt them down, cut their supply and sealed their exits, and within a few months the host dispersed; Wang Bo himself disappeared, and neither the official histories nor the Comprehensive Mirror leaves any account of what became of him, nor any report of the battle, of prisoners or of losses in this campaign. Only three facts can be established: the rising, its suppression and its ending. For the Sui this was a successful suppression, but not a solution: it showed that villagers could raise several tens of thousands within a matter of weeks with nothing but a song, and it showed that the Sui military system could not hold down answers breaking out at the same time in Qi and Lu, in Hebei and in Jiangnan. And precisely because the suppression succeeded, the risings in other places were able to follow one another while the court's attention was fixed on the north; by Daye 9 more than twenty commanderies were in revolt, and by the last years of Daye the separatist states of Wagang, of Dou Jiande, of Du Fuwei and of Liu Hei had appeared, and the Sui house held out among these powers until the first year of Wude. The Corinthian helmet on the card fits the moment exactly: it is seventh-century Greek work, the face open all the way across, and the man who wears it can only live by his formation. The rebels of Shandong in 611 had no helmet, but they had a song and the ties of the same village, which is a form of collective protection just the same. The only difference is that by then the Sui had no institutions left that could enrol such a company into any order of battle at all.
